reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. Gate 1: errorHandler is actively registered as Express middleware in src/index.ts:83 (non-test caller exists, exported middleware). Gate 2: no trust_assumptions defined in BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json; attack entry point is any unauthenticated or authenticated HTTP request that triggers an unhandled exception — no trusted-source restriction applies. Gate 3: src/middleware/ is explicitly in-scope and the scope JSON even lists 'Error messages may leak internal details in non-production mode' as a key security concern. Code at L16 confirms the defect: `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` evaluates to `true` when NODE_ENV is undefined, so err.message is always included in the HTTP 500 response body under the 'details' field. An attacker can trigger this via any HTTP endpoint (e.g., malformed request body, DB connection failure) against a deployment launched without NODE_ENV set (e.g., direct `node dist/index.js`), causing the raw err.message to be returned in the response and leaking internal implementation details. Severity Medium is appropriate for information disclosure with a realistic but deployment-dependent precondition.
